title: The Octonauts and the whale.
lines: Deep under the sea, among the coral and the fish, floats a big underwater base.
It looks like an octopus, with long arms.
He's a big, strong polar bear with a blue cap.
Kwazii is an orange cat with an eye patch.
He's a bit of a pirate.
He loves adventure and he always says: Ahoy!
He always has his doctor's bag with him, with plasters and bandages.
He's a bit scared, but when someone is ill, he's very brave.
And Professor Inkling is an octopus with glasses.
He knows everything about the sea.
He lives in the library, among the books.
One morning the alarm goes off.
A message appears on the big screen.
There's a whale in the bay.
They jump into their submarine, the Gup-A.
It's a fast, blue submarine, shaped like a fish.
On the way Professor Inkling tells them about whales over the radio.
Whales are the biggest animals in the world, he says.
They have to go up to the surface to breathe, through a hole on their back.
And when they do, they spray a big fountain.
In the bay they see her.
She's as long as three buses in a row.
She's lying in the shallow water, close to the beach.
If we don't do anything, she'll end up on dry land, says the captain.
And then she won't be able to swim.
Peso swims over to the whale.
She's tired, he says, and a bit scared.
She just needs to get back to deep water.
She's too heavy to push, he says.
Then he looks at the water.
The tide will come back in later.
We don't have that much time.
They call to each other over very long distances.
Maybe her family can help her!
He finds a recording of a whale song.
They play it through the Gup-A's loudspeakers.
Far away, in the deep sea, other whales hear it.
And they swim to the bay.
They swim back and forth in front of the bay.
They make big waves with their tails.
The water flows in, around the stuck whale.
They all spray a big fountain, as a thank you.
Back in the Octopod Professor Inkling writes something in his big book.
